text:
A: Hey! Lisa, is it? Daniel. How you doing?
B: Hiya, Daniel! I'm all right, thanks. Bit frazzled, all these calls, I keep forgetting who I've told what.
A: Ha, I know, it's like speed dating but everyone's got a dog. Where are you?
B: Ipswich. I work near Felixstowe, at the port. Freight forwarding, so I do all the paperwork for the containers.
A: No way, Felixstowe. We've got a client with a couple of warehouses out that way, I did the leases last year. Off the A14.
B: Oh, the A14! Don't get me started, it's a nightmare.
A: The A14, yeah, I've heard the A14's a killer. I've only got the Northern line to moan about, to be fair.
B: Is that bad?
A: Honestly, it's like a sardine tin with delays. But it's twenty minutes, so I can't really complain. What's your commute?
B: Half hour if I'm lucky. Then I forget my lanyard and have to buzz in. Every week. I'm useless, me.
A: Ha, I'd be the same without my calendar. I'm a solicitor, commercial property. I basically live by reminders.
B: I said that! When I saw your picture, I thought, he's one of those ones who always knows where his paperwork is.
A: Guilty. Colour-coded trackers. My wife thinks it's tragic.
B: I've got sticky notes. All over the screen. And half-drunk mugs of tea. My manager just sort of looks at it and walks away.
A: But it works, though, right? You find stuff?
B: Mostly! I just ring people and say, sorry, can you send it again, and they do 'cause they like me.
A: Honestly, that's the real skill. That's what I do at client drinks. Remember everyone's names, their kids' schools. People do favours for people they like.
B: That's it, isn't it. My mum always said you catch more flies with honey.
A: My mum'd say the same. She was a school receptionist, knew every kid in the building.
B: Oh, I've thought about that, a school office! For the holidays. I've never looked into it properly, though.
A: You'd be great at it, to be fair. Do you travel much?
B: Package stuff, mostly. Lanzarote, Crete. I always book late. But I went to New York for my fortieth. Still talk about it. Dean's sick of hearing.
A: New York for your fortieth, that's class. Where'd you stay?
B: Erm, Times Square, ish. A tiny room, but the view! What about you?
A: We did Méribel this year, skiing. Loved it. And I'll always ask for an upgrade at check-in, it's a bit of a hobby.
B: Do they give you one?
A: About half the time. You've just got to ask nicely. Same as your sticky notes, really, it's all
